headline: AI Automation Engineer | Claude Code, AI Agents, MCP Servers & n8n | Python, TypeScript & API Integrations
professional_summary: AI Automation Engineer with 3.5 years in Python and workflow automation, including 2.5 years shipping Claude API integrations and self-hosted n8n workflows for US healthcare, US legal marketing, and Australian e-commerce teams. Builds AI agents, MCP servers, and Claude Code tooling (subagents, hooks, Agent Skills), gating client-facing drafts behind versioned system prompts, evals, and human review.

bullets.text: Built an n8n pipeline on US-region AWS with retries and error workflows, using Claude tool-use schemas to extract payer, referral, and visit reason from 1,900 yearly web forms and OCR'd faxes at 96% staff-verified accuracy.

Cut median business-hours first-reply time on web inquiries from 13 to 6 minutes in 3 months with a Claude routing agent that posts Google Chat alerts without PHI and feeds HIPAA-enabled GoHighLevel pipelines.
Developed an in-house TypeScript MCP server whose 7 scheduling, eligibility, and intake-status tools give the routing agent only record IDs and status codes, replacing staff lookups across 3 systems.

Masked direct identifiers (name, DOB, phone, member ID) in form and OCR text before each Claude API call under a BAA, re-linking results by record ID and logging every request for HIPAA audit controls.

Raised staff approval of first-draft replies from 72% to 91% by revising versioned system prompts against a Python eval harness that scores 250 drafts per release on accuracy, tone, and escalation rules.

Standardized PHI-free n8n QA in Claude Code with a review subagent, a deploy-gate hook, and Agent Skills, shipping runbook documentation with each of 14 releases and shortening delivery from 9 to 4 working days.

experiences.company_archetype: Personal Injury Law Firm Marketing Agency (Texas, US)

bullets.text: Automated case-intake triage for 9 personal-injury firms with an n8n and Claude tool-use agent that classified 3,200 web leads by case type (motor vehicle, trucking, premises), misclassifying under 3%.
Flagged adverse-party names for each firm's conflict check and incident dates nearing Texas's two-year statute of limitations as structured JSON, cutting lead screening from 25 to 8 minutes.
Shipped, as sole engineer, the agency's first read-only Python MCP server over its PostgreSQL intake database, then onboarded account managers in Claude Desktop with a plain-language guide.
Routed every AI-drafted follow-up through a Slack approval queue for client-firm intake staff, where 84% of 2,100 drafts passed unedited.

Audited the CX queue, then built self-hosted n8n workflows on Docker, triggered by Gorgias HTTP integrations, that triaged 2,400 monthly tickets for a 6-person team using Shopify GraphQL Admin API return status.
Enriched 1,150 variant listings via Claude tool use against one JSON schema, cutting catalog updates from 3 days to 5 hours per drop.
Reduced refund resolution from 4.2 to 1.6 days by sending Shopify return/refund webhooks via REST APIs to Gorgias and a Google Sheets log.

experiences.company_archetype: Philippine Data Science Organization & Industry-Partner Engagement

bullets.text: Researched and scored 240 construction firms for a construction-supply partner, yielding 180 qualified accounts and 18 quote requests.
Wrote Python scripts to scrape directories, fill contact gaps, and flag duplicate firms in Google Sheets, saving 4 hours of list work weekly.

projects.name: n8n Workflow Guard Skill Pack
projects.summary: A PreToolUse Bash hook that denies n8n import:workflow and API pushes until a validator clears the exported JSON of missing error workflows, inline secrets, and unlisted community nodes. Agent Skills hold the fix steps. Caught 37 risky changes across 3 Git repositories.

projects.name: Intake Reply Eval Kit
projects.summary: A pytest suite that replays 120 synthetic intake scenarios against Claude prompts, grades replies with structured outputs, and fails the GitHub Actions check on regressions, running in under 4 minutes per pull request.
